transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, doctor. Mostly I'm here because... well, I just don't sleep right anymore. I'll get in bed and just lie there a long time. And then, if I do finally get to sleep, I end up waking up from bad dreams, or even just little noises. Once I'm up like that, I just can't seem to settle back down to get any real rest.
During the day, have you been feeling persistently sad, low, or hopeless?
Well, no, I wouldn't say that. I ain't really sad or hopeless. I mean, I get pretty worn out during the day from not sleeping right, but... no, my mood is mostly alright, just regular.
When you are lying in bed unable to sleep, what is typically going through your mind?

Nothing much, really. I ain't lying there thinking about anything in particular. Just... well, just wishing I was asleep, mostly. I'll just be staring in the dark, waiting to drift off. It's not like my mind is racing with a bunch of thoughts or anything like that. I'm just awake when I don't want to be.
When you wake up during the night, do you ever notice yourself gasping for air, snoring loudly, or feeling like your legs are restless or uncomfortable?

No, I ain't noticed anything like that. I don't wake up gasping or nothing. And my legs feel fine, they don't bother me. Like I said, it's mostly just bad dreams or hearing a noise that wakes me up, not my breathing or my legs.
How many nights a week, on average, does this difficulty with your sleep happen, and how long has this been going on for?

Well, it's pretty much every night. And, uh... it's been going on since I had that ladder accident. That was about a year and seven months ago, give or take. Ever since then, my sleep just hasn't been right.
Since that accident, do you find yourself having any unwanted, vivid memories or flashbacks of what happened?

Yeah, I do. It ain't all the time, but... well, if I hear metal scraping, or even just if I'm driving by and see a ladder leaning up against somebody's house, it just hits me. The whole thing jumps right back into my head. It's like I'm right back under there again, just... stuck, waiting for somebody to come help me.
